name: Lizard
oneLiner: Firecracker sandboxes at a flat hourly price per size, plus an app platform for whatever the agent builds.
whatItIs: Lizard is a cloud platform with two halves. Sandboxes are Firecracker microVMs for running agent code, sold in three fixed sizes at a flat hourly price. An app platform deploys a repository, with managed Postgres, Redis and S3-compatible storage.

The docs describe the sandbox half first and treat app deployment as the second step, once the agent has built something. The two halves are billed on different meters, which is the most confusing thing about the product.
The self-serve plans are Pro at $19 a month, Pro 5x at $99 and Pro 20x at $499; each includes its own fee back as usage across the whole platform, and the bigger two raise the sandbox limits.
whoFor: Agent builders who want cheap per-hour machines with generous pause and snapshot semantics, and who may want to deploy the result on the same platform.
isolation: Firecracker microVM with its own guest kernel, commands run as root by default, Linux only. Docker inside a sandbox, systemd and nested virtualisation are not documented.
sizes: Four fixed sizes: Mini 1 vCPU / 2 GB / 5 GB, Small 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 20 GB, Medium 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 40 GB, Large 8 vCPU / 16 GB / 80 GB. Mini starts only from four templates and takes no volume. No custom size and no live resize. Volumes add 1 to 50 GB at `/workspace`.

billing.model: Three plans, Pro at $19, Pro 5x at $99 and Pro 20x at $499 a month, each including its fee as usage; sandboxes are a flat hourly price per size.
billing.meter: Per second while running, idle time included, at $0.0081 / $0.0162 / $0.0324 / $0.0648 an hour for Mini / Small / Medium / Large. Volumes bill per GB-month on used space.
billing.stopped: Paused compute is $0, and no storage charge for a paused sandbox's disk or memory is published. A stopped sandbox is deleted, so only volumes and snapshots remain.
billing.planFee: $19 (Pro), $99 (Pro 5x) or $499 (Pro 20x) a month, each coming back as the same amount of usage. Unused usage does not carry over.
billing.minimum: $19 a month is the floor. The 7-day trial includes $5 of usage, needs a card, and runs 1 Small and 2 Mini at a time for at most an hour each.

A.headline: $19 a month (the plan floor)
A.shape: Small (2 vCPU / 4 GB / 20 GB), deleted after each task
notes: The size exists exactly, so no substitution is needed.
Pro has no limit on sandbox starts, so 1,000 tasks can run in a day within 40 vCPU at once.

B.headline: $25.05 or $47.30 a month
B.shape: No size is 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 50 GB: Medium has 40 GB of disk, Large has 80 GB but 8 vCPU.
notes: Option one matches the CPU and RAM exactly and splits the disk across two filesystems.
Volumes bill on used space, not allocated size.
B.flag: Both options over-deliver something: the first adds a volume, the second doubles CPU and RAM to get the disk.

C.headline: $19 a month (the plan floor)
C.shape: Small (2 vCPU / 4 GB / 20 GB), 90 running hours
notes: Small now has 20 GB of disk, so no volume is needed.
Stopped here means killed, which deletes the sandbox disk: pause instead, or keep files on a volume.
C.flag: Pausing instead of stopping keeps the whole disk and memory, at no published storage charge.

facts.label: Legal entity
facts.value: Dragon Labs LLC, doing business as Lizard. Delaware law, with a Portland, Oregon mailing address.

source.quote: We are Dragon Labs LLC, doing business as Lizard

facts.label: History
facts.value: First public SDK release 24 June 2026 and first blog post 31 July 2026. No founding date is published.

facts.label: Funding
facts.value: No announced round, amount or investor list. A directory labels the stage Seed.

facts.label: Headcount
facts.value: Two, per LinkedIn. Yura Dubinin is named as co-founder and president; Mikhail Erin co-authors the blog.

facts.label: Status and SLA
facts.value: 99.95% platform uptime. No sandbox component is monitored, and no SLA exists outside Enterprise.

facts.label: Certification
facts.value: No SOC 2 report yet; no ISO 27001 or HIPAA claim is published.

well: A flat hourly price per size with a $19 plan, billed per second including idle time.
Snapshots that keep memory and processes, and forks of 1–100 copies.
A dashboard-first first machine with a hosted MCP server for assistants.
badly: A long job from the SDK or CLI: the default lifetime is five minutes and there is no idle timer.
Anything outside /workspace that must survive a stop, which deletes the rest of the disk.
SSH-dependent tooling: there is no SSH protocol, so scp and port forwarding do not work.

usability.dashboard: Yes, and it creates sandboxes without code: pick a template, region, size and lifetime, then pause, resume, open a terminal or browse volumes.
usability.withoutCode: Partly. Creating a sandbox is click-driven, and the terminal tab gives you a shell. Running an agent, taking a snapshot, forking and attaching a volume are CLI or SDK only, and a card is needed to start the trial.
usability.signup: GitHub or Google, then a card through Stripe Checkout for the 7-day trial. Nothing is charged during the trial. There is no free tier to use without a plan.
usability.docs: Unusually candid: per-page updated dates, test-status notes saying what was and was not verified, raw Markdown twins. Support is email and Discord. The status page covers the platform but not sandbox capacity.
tripsUp: The default lifetime is 5 minutes from the SDK and CLI, and never from the dashboard or raw API.
Stop means delete, including everything outside /workspace.
Everything interesting beyond creating a sandbox needs a terminal.
The card comes before the product.
Two bills in one number: apps are metered per vCPU-second, sandboxes are flat per hour, a 6.2× gap for the same capacity.
Overage charges arrive automatically with no spending cap.

caveats.issue: Snapshot storage has no published price
caveats.detail: Restores are priced at the source's hourly rate, but stored snapshots have no rate anywhere on the pricing or billing pages.

caveats.issue: Stop deletes the sandbox and its disk
caveats.detail: There is no stopped-but-restartable state. Only `/workspace` volumes and snapshots survive, and there is no trash or recycle bin.

caveats.issue: Two default lifetimes that contradict each other
caveats.detail: Five minutes from the SDK and CLI, no expiry from the raw API and dashboard. A beginner following the CLI docs can lose work without warning.

evidence.quote: Five minutes by default from the SDK and CLI; no expiration by default from the raw API and dashboard
Pick a lifetime under Delete after: 15 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours, 1 day, 7 days, or Never (the default).

caveats.issue: Docker inside a sandbox is not documented
caveats.detail: Neither is systemd, nested virtualisation, kernel feature support or CPU architecture. Treat all of them as unverified.
Overage is charged automatically in steps from $20 up to $1,000, with no ceiling. The docs say so explicitly.

caveats.issue: The runtime and billing model changed without notice
caveats.detail: On 30 September the docs described one fixed 4 vCPU / 4096 MiB sandbox in shared-kernel Kubernetes pods, billed on measured usage. By 13 October the pricing page listed Firecracker microVMs at flat per-size rates, from $0.0162 an hour. The changelog and blog do not mention the switch. Whether anyone's bill rose cannot be told, because the old usage rates were never published. Older sandboxes keep usage-based billing.

caveats.issue: The pricing page and the docs list different sizes
caveats.detail: The pricing page adds a Nano size (0.5 vCPU / 1 GB / 5 GB, $0.00405 an hour), gives Mini 10 GB of disk and says volumes go up to 100 GB. The limits, SDK and volumes docs list no Nano, give Mini 5 GB and cap volumes at 50 GB. This guide follows the docs.

evidence.quote: Nano0.5 vCPU · 1 GB RAM · 5 GB disk
New volumes allow **1 to 50 GB**, in whole GB, with **5 GB** as the default.

strengths: Pause keeps memory, processes and the whole disk, and paused compute is $0.
Snapshots capture memory, processes and the whole disk, and restore into a new sandbox.
Fork 1–100 copies of a running sandbox with memory, source paused only briefly.
A dashboard that creates sandboxes without code.
2 TB of sandbox egress a month included, with no per-GB charge.
